title: Cvetličarna Pirc, ena linija
gapNote: The drawing is the pilot florist motif (secateurs and a rose stem), drawn in several strokes, not one continuous line; ornament/continuous-line and composition/hero/drawn-object (stance signatures) don't exist, so the line can't run on from the drawing into a rule, the timeline or the map, which is the stance's point. Its stroke is fixed in the drawing's own units, so at six columns it is thin and at phone width thinner still; a decor element has no stroke weight. There is no second florist drawing (a tulip, a peony, a bunch), so the seasons are a plain timeline list with no line drawing of each flower, and the timeline's leads sit tight against their rings. The client's handwritten notes can only be referenced, not shown: there is no handwritten-label type treatment.
sources: T Etiketa (one drawn object, airy white)
